what_this_measures: Employers headquartered in the EU27, the United Kingdom, Switzerland or Norway that announced a funding round or a leadership change between 2026-08-01 and 2026-08-31, on the ANNOUNCEMENT date, broken out by country. The first European reference set; there is no earlier one to compare it with.
method: Assembled on 2026-09-12 by 4 INDEPENDENT research passes (europe_cee, europe_central_south, europe_fr_it, europe_north), each run in isolation from the others and forbidden from consulting this tracker, its database, its repository or asktherecruiter.com; discovery was public web search and the publishers' own pages, in local languages as well as English, walked chronologically inside the window and taken in that order. Every candidate row was fetched by the pass that proposed it, then fetched AGAIN mechanically from this machine before sealing (HTTP 200 and the employer's name on the page, or dropped as unreachable), and then put to two independent referees (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 and openai/gpt-4o) with the protocol's own event definition and an excerpt of the mechanically fetched page. Only rows both referees accepted entered the set; every verdict is recorded in analysis/recall/2026-08-eu-v1-labels.json. Nothing was added, edited or removed after matching began. No country may exceed 28% of the set, so the figure is a European one and not a London one.
held_out: Sampled independently of our own coverage. No pass saw our database, our stored rows or our collector list, and no pass could cite an aggregator, a deal database or another tracker.
caveats: Most countries carry only a few events, so a single country cell is an indication and not a rate; the country table is a work list.
The population is the EU27 plus the United Kingdom, Switzerland and Norway, by headquarters. Turkey, Ukraine, the western Balkans and the Caucasus are not in it.
This measures two of the four kinds of signal the tracker collects, funding rounds and leadership changes. Pay and ways-of-working signals are not tested here.
Every row was accepted by two AI referees reading a fetched excerpt, not by a person. The labels file keeps every verdict.

Rows a pass verified but which refused a second, mechanical fetch from this machine were dropped as unreachable and are listed in the file, so countries whose press blocks fetchers are under-represented.
Funding events with amount_disclosed=false carry no figure because the publisher stated none.

sampling_by_pass.europe_cee: I enumerated country by country from 2026-08-01 forward using WebSearch in English and local languages (Polish, Czech, Romanian, Turkish, Russian, Ukrainian, Hungarian, Slovak, Slovene, Croatian, Bulgarian, Georgian, Azerbaijani), then read the funding and news category pages of MamStartup, CzechCrunch, The Recursive (country tags), Webrazzi, Digital Business Kazakhstan, Spot.uz, ArcticStartup, Romania Insider, Bankier and Stockwatch ESPI feeds. Every row kept was fetched by me and the excerpt is copied from the fetched page. The search budget ran out after the first sweep, so coverage is a partial file: Poland, Bulgaria, Lithuania, Hungary, Croatia, Turkey and Uzbekistan carry rows; Czechia, Slovakia, Romania, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, Serbia, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan have none because the pages I could still fetch returned nothing dated August or refused (Romania Insider answered 429 three times, ArcticStartup and AIN 403, KASE and Nasdaq Baltic listings rendered empty, several category pages 404). Leadership rows are two Polish exchange filings; the leadership searches for Turkey, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Hungary, Romania and the Baltics surfaced only pre-window or state-agency appointments. Dropped: Zynt (published April), Astute (headquarters not stated, likely not Serbia), Nace.AI and Perceptis (Silicon Valley headquartered), Lasken AI and Codeplain (July), Veeda AI (404), LITILIT (both publishers blocked), Nuclearelectrica CEO exit (429), Prague Airport chair (appointment predates the window), Imperio ASI (September), Kazatomprom and Nasdaq Baltic pages (2021 and 2023). Three kept rows carry excerpts shorter than 300 characters because the fetch tool refused to reproduce more of the page; they are flagged in the verified field. EUR converted at about 1.16 USD.
sampling_by_pass.europe_central_south: I enumerated country by country from 2026-08-01 using local language searches and then fetched the original publisher for each candidate. For Germany I used the deutsche-startups.de monthly investment roundups (the 2026-09-04 piece covers August and named NavVis, Oceanloop, Moss and Flip) and EQS filings found via onvista, taking Moss, Flip, Oceanloop, MOBOTIX and Heidelberger Druckmaschinen in date order and stopping at the cap of five (NavVis was left out only because the cap was reached). For Switzerland I walked the startupticker.ch Financing category listing for August in date order and took Zerolook, Aisot, UpGrid and BitVault, then the SMG Swiss Marketplace Group CEO succession from the company newsroom. Austria came from an EQS notice on ots.at (wienerberger), Spain from the national and business press (FuVeX, after El Referente returned 403), Portugal from ECO (Neuraspace), Cyprus from the Omilia newsroom. I could not verify a single row for France, Italy, Greece or Malta: Maddyness and French Tech Journal show no August 2026 items in their indexes, StartupItalia and BeBeez return 403 on every article (HypeSound, Bynario, Klaaryo and Qomodo were surfaced but could not be fetched), and Greek and Maltese searches produced only out of window appointments. My web search budget ran out at that point, so the pass stops at 14 verified rows, 4 of them leadership and 10 funding, 12 small and 2 large, across filing, press_release, trade_press and national_news. Dropped rows are listed with reasons: several were outside the window (Endesa April, Beelzebub 27 July, Urbaser 3 September, tonies 2025, ARAG Greece January), several were unfetchable, and two were not qualifying roles (a newspaper director, a state university director general). Some evidence excerpts fall slightly short of 300 characters where the fetcher returned only a short passage; those are marked in the verified field. USD conversions use about 1.17 per EUR and 1.25 per CHF.
sampling_by_pass.europe_fr_it: I worked country by country from 2026-08-01 forward using WebSearch and WebFetch only. For France I enumerated the Frenchweb levee de fonds rubric (pages 1 and 2), the Journal des Entreprises nominations carnet, ActusNews, GlobeNewswire FR, Business Wire FR, Boursorama and La Tribune; Frenchweb's August listing yielded two rows, of which only ARCSPACE (26 Aug) is a French employer, Sapiom being a US company covered in French. The JdE carnet listing jumped from 23 July to 3 September, and the wire searches returned only July and September nominations, so France closed at one row. Usine Nouvelle's nomination page returned 403. For Italy I used Milano Finanza, Teleborsa (the Borsa Italiana news feed) and BeBeez, which gave PagoPa, ENAV and e-Novia; the two Italian funding candidates (Beelzebub, SylloTips) were dated July 2026 and 2025, and CyLock's BeBeez page and Scientifica VC release both failed to fetch. For Portugal I walked ECO's startups topic page chronologically and verified Neuraspace, Defined.ai and GalgoSheets. For Spain, El Referente returned 403, GuruSup turned out to be an April round, PageMind and Tripjoin were July, and the only in window item (Migaya Arte Sano, Gijon) yielded fewer than 300 verbatim characters, so I dropped it. For Greece I searched ekathimerini, Naftemporiki, Capital.gr, Startupper and Growthfund in Greek and English and found no in window event; the Growthfund ETAD page was from 2023. For Malta the MaltaCEOs front page listed no company executive appointment dated August 2026, and Times of Malta searches surfaced nothing. I stopped at the tool budget with 7 verified rows: 4 leadership, 3 funding, 3 source types, all three funding rows small, three leadership rows large.
sampling_by_pass.europe_north: I worked country by country, GB first, then IE, NL, BE, LU, DK, SE, NO, FI, enumerating August 2026 from the start of the month forward. For GB I read UKTN's weekly funding roundups for 3 to 7, 10 to 14 and 17 to 21 August and took the smallest rounds in the order they appeared, and read Investegate RNS notices for CFO and CEO changes, plus BusinessCloud for private company appointments. For IE I used the Irish Times, RTE and Silicon Republic. For NL, Tech.eu and GlobeNewswire company announcements. For BE, Made in (regional business press) and EU-Startups headlines. For DK, GlobeNewswire Nasdaq Copenhagen announcements and Tech.eu. For SE, company newsrooms (SBB, Coop, eComID) and Tech.eu. For NO, Tech.eu, the Blastr newsroom, the Oslo Bors NewsWeb API and the Orkla newsroom. For FI, VTT and GlobeNewswire Nasdaq Helsinki releases. Local language searches in Swedish, Dutch, Norwegian, Danish and Finnish surfaced several rows. My search budget ran out after the first two rounds, so the remaining enumeration was done by fetching archive and listing pages directly; many outlets (EU-Startups, ArcticStartup, Sifted, Tech Funding News, Cision Nordic) return 403 to the fetcher, and several national dailies (DI, Borsen, Kauppalehti, HS, FD, De Tijd, Independent) block it entirely. I could not verify a single Luxembourg row: the only August candidates were a grant, a chief product officer appointment, a Jersey headquartered firm, and a Vanksen managing director story whose Paperjam and Delano pages print only the current date, so LU has zero rows and the LU minimum is unmet. I dropped rows announced outside the window (Videndum, Quartr, Fairstone, Helix, Unilin), rows whose pages could not be fetched (Motion, Artwod, DFDS chair), and one where the fetcher would not return a verbatim excerpt (YouGov). I reached 22 verified rows against a target of 26, with 13 leadership rows and 12 small rows across four source types.
